fine_lines.title: sneaked vs snuck
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الكلمتان صحيحتان كماضٍ للفعل sneak. sneaked هي الشكل الأقدم والأشهر في بريطانيا، وsnuck شائعة جدًا في أمريكا. في الدرس قالت آنا: I have never snuck … ثم: I sneaked down an air duct.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both are correct past forms of "sneak". "Sneaked" is older and common in British English; "snuck" is very common in American English. Anna says both: "I have never snuck …" and "I sneaked down an air duct."

examples.sentence: He snuck out of the room.
She sneaked a look at the answers.

fine_lines.title: I did it vs I've done it
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I did it = الماضي البسيط، حدث وانتهى (وغالبًا يُذكر الوقت). I've done it = المضارع التام، النتيجة مهمة الآن ولا نذكر وقتًا محددًا. لا نستخدم المضارع التام مع yesterday أو last week.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I did it" = past simple: finished, often with a time. "I've done it" = present perfect: the result matters now; no specific time. Don't use the present perfect with "yesterday" or "last week".

examples.sentence: I've cracked the code! My brain hurts.

fine_lines.title: breath vs breathe
fine_lines.explanation_ar: breath اسم (نَفَس) وتُنطق /breθ/. breathe فعل (يتنفس) وتُنطق /briːð/.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Breath" is a noun, said /breθ/. "Breathe" is a verb, said /briːð/.

grammar.title: Present perfect vs past simple
grammar.explanation_ar:
• المضارع التام (have/has + p.p.) للتجربة في الحياة أو لنتيجة مهمة الآن، بدون وقت محدد: I have never snuck down an air duct. Have you ever cracked a code? I've cracked the code!
• الماضي البسيط لحدث انتهى في وقت معروف أو في قصة: I did it! I sneaked down an air duct. That was a little uncomfortable.
قاعدة سهلة: إذا ذكرت متى (yesterday, at 10, last week) استخدم الماضي البسيط.
grammar.explanation_en:
• Present perfect (have/has + past participle) for life experience or a result that matters now, with no specific time: I have never snuck down an air duct. Have you ever cracked a code? I've cracked the code!
• Past simple for a finished action at a known time or in a story: I did it! I sneaked down an air duct. That was a little uncomfortable.
Easy rule: if you say when (yesterday, at 10, last week), use the past simple.
examples: I have never snuck down an air duct.
Have you ever cracked a code?
I did it! I sneaked down an air duct.

grammar.title: have to: necessity
grammar.explanation_ar: have to / has to + الفعل الأساسي = يجب، لابد (ضرورة). Spies have to be in good shape. مع he/she/it نقول has to. السؤال: Do spies have to …? النفي: You don't have to …
grammar.explanation_en: have to / has to + base verb = it is necessary. Spies have to be in good shape. Use "has to" with he/she/it. Question: Do spies have to …? Negative: You don't have to … (= it is not necessary).
examples: Spies have to be in really good shape.
She has to be back by noon.
Do spies have to be in good shape?
You don't have to come early.

questions.explanation_en: have + never + past participle: I have never cracked.
